$comment: What this server was built against, and the gate that keeps it honest.
arcnow-io/sdk is NOT PUBLISHED TO NPM. package.json therefore depends on it
by path - `file:../sdk/typescript` - and npm links the sibling checkout's
WORKING TREE into node_modules. That is the whole reason this file exists.
A registry dependency is a version number that resolves to immutable bytes;
a path dependency resolves to whatever somebody happens to have checked out,
which may be a branch, a rebase, or an edit made five minutes ago. Nothing
about that fails loudly: the server compiles, the tool descriptions still
say what they said, and the call that reaches the chain is encoded by code
nobody in this repository has read.
So the SDK is pinned the same way arcnow-io/sdk pins arcnow-io/contracts,
and scripts/check-pins.sh enforces five things, with preflight.sh running it
straight after the install:
0. sdk.commit is a full 40-hex commit, never a ref that resolves to
whatever it names today.
1. package.json still depends on the SDK BY PATH. A `file:` specifier
quietly becoming `^0.1.0` would resolve to whatever the registry serves
under that name - today, nothing; tomorrow, anyone's package.
2. The linked node_modules/@arcnow/sdk really is that sibling checkout,
carries sdk.version, and its dist/ is EXACTLY what its working tree
compiles to - checked by compiling it again. This server imports dist/,
so a dist/ left over from an older checkout runs old code under new
hashes. That is not hypothetical: it is the state the sibling checkout
was in when the pin moved off ac52eaa, with no dist/pool.js at all.
3. The sibling's WORKING TREE hashes to surface_sha256, with no surface
file unpinned. The linked directory is the working tree, not the commit,
so an uncommitted edit or an uncommitted new module in the SDK is code
this server runs and no git ref names.
4. sdk.commit exists, is on sdk.branch, and carries exactly the pinned
files with the pinned bytes - the only check that can see the hashes
belong to the commit named. It also reports, without failing, when the
SDK has moved past the pin and whether the surface changed in the
interval; a pin is supposed to lag, and reading that diff is a
person's job.
WHICH FILES ARE PINNED IS A RULE, NOT A LIST: networks.json,
typescript/package.json, and every file under typescript/src except
typescript/src/errors/. A module the SDK adds is surface the moment it
exists. The generated ABIs are inside the rule because they encode every
call; the generated networks.json because it is the copy the SDK actually
compiles its ADDRESSES from - the one input where being out of date means
sending money to the wrong account. typescript/src/errors/ is outside it:
message prose behind a surface index.ts already pins, where pinning would
make every improved error message a false alarm here.
MOVING THE PIN is a commit of its own: check the SDK out at the commit,
build it, run scripts/check-pins.sh --record (which records sdk.commit and
every surface hash from HEAD, and refuses an edit no commit carries), update
sdk.why, run scripts/preflight.sh, and say in the message what changed in
the SDK surface and what it meant for the tools. A tool description that
still promises what an older SDK did is how a model ends up telling somebody
the wrong price.

why: arcnow-io/sdk main at 8aa50f4 - the merge commit of arcnow-io/sdk#9 (multi-quote), whose tree is
the head that was tested, 61b4798. The SDK for the multi-quote contract stack, pinning
arcnow-io/contracts main 327f45b (bonding-curve@3, launchpad@3, quote-registry@1, fee hook @3).
Its networks.json records the v3 multi-quote stack AS DEPLOYED on Arc testnet on 2026-09-15:
launchpad 0x3e4f0291...b1240, arcnowPlatform 0xa78b737d...ea47a, quoteRegistry 0x72405d10...bb9b3,
every contractVersion at 3.x, deployedAtBlock 62226550, contractsCommit 327f45b, and EURC
0x89b50855...9d72a (6 decimals) among its quoteTokens. THIS SERVER RESTATES NO ADDRESS: it reads
them from that preset, or from a document the operator names in ARCNOW_MCP_NETWORK_FILE. Moving
this pin is therefore how the addresses this server sends money to change.
What this server uses from it: QuoteAmount and QuoteTokenInfo, which label every
amount with its own quote; CurveState.quoteToken; quoteIn/quoteSpent/quoteOut/
feeQuote on quotes and results; Pool.quoteToken() and quoteIsCurrency0(); LaunchQuote
{quoteToken, launchFee, initialBuy, totalCost, nativeValue, tradeFee}; approvalTxHash
on buy, pool-buy and launch results; client.quoteRegistry.list(),
client.quoteToken(info).spendState and client.quoteTokenInfo; findQuoteToken and
resolveNetwork for ARCNOW_MCP_NETWORK_FILE; platforms.curveParametersFor; and the
codes QuoteTokenMismatch and QuoteAmountNotRepresentable, plus the 3.x version gates
that refuse the retired 2.x contracts as UnknownCurveVersion. Those contracts are no longer
arcnow.io's stack - their platform was deregistered in the 2026-09-15 reset - but they are still
on Arc testnet, and every token launched on them still answers VERSION() from them.
Also used: QuoteTransferOutOfGas, the empty revert of contracts#23's gas guard on ERC-20
fee-share transfers, surfaced by name; erc20GasLimit, which raises a caller's ERC-20 gas limit to
the estimate plus max(20%, 150,000) and keeps a higher one (this server sends a graduating ERC-20
buy max(caller, GRADUATION_GAS_LIMIT)); and withPoolQuoteTransferHeadroom, which gives an ERC-20 pool
swap the estimate plus max(20%, 400,000) (contracts security review L-1).
Moved from 20af267 (the pre-merge head of #9). What changed in the surface in between is the
address record and nothing else: networks.json took the deployed v3 addresses, versions,
deployedAtBlock and contractsCommit, and gained EURC; the shipped curve template moved its
snapshot to the new platform at platform-config@3.0.0, read at block 62227596, with the same six
wads. No exported type, function or error code moved, so no tool description changed with it.
Before that: c89ced9 (main, the 2.x single-stack SDK), by way of 6773e38, 539c090, a06de48,
e36547e and 20af267 on multi-quote.

$comment: Restated here so this repository can be read alone, and asserted against
the SDK's networks.json by the test suite so the two can never drift into
disagreeing. Addresses are NOT restated: they live in the SDK's
networks.json and are read from it at run time. Two copies of an address
list is how one of them ends up wrong.
Arc's gas currency IS USDC and msg.value is an 18-decimal integer. The
6-decimal figure belongs to the ERC-20 interface predeploy, which is the
same asset and does not pay for gas. Everything this server prints says
which of the two it means.
fork_block is the Arc testnet block the fork proof forks at. Pinned, so
anvil caches the state it fetches (test/fork/support/chain.ts mounts its
cache) and a repeat run asks the rate-limited public endpoint for nothing
it already has. The proof DEPLOYS ITS OWN 3.x stack onto the fork with the
SDK's scripts/fork-deploy-stack.sh and points the server at it through
ARCNOW_MCP_NETWORK_FILE, so no arcnow.io address on the forked chain is
read and the block does not have to be after the 2026-09-15 reset that
deployed the live v3 stack (62226550). What it does have to carry is what
the proof borrows from Arc: EURC, the v4 PoolManager, the v4 router, and
real EOAs in the 400 blocks before it to impersonate. 61926859 carries all
four and is already in the cache, which on a rate-limited endpoint is worth
more than resembling today's tip. ARCNOW_MCP_FORK_BLOCK overrides it;
"latest" forks the tip.

toolchains.$comment: Exact, never a range and never auto-detected - the same node release arcnow-io/sdk pins, because this server is compiled against that SDK's sources.

images.$comment: Pinned, never 'latest'. The anvil the fork proof runs: the same Foundry image arcnow-io/sdk and arcnow-io/e2e-tests pin, so a fork that behaves differently in one of them behaves differently for a reason somebody chose.
